overview.intro:
Chapter 51 covers wool and animal hair from the fleece to woven cloth: **greasy, scoured and carbonized wool** (5101), **cashmere, camel, alpaca, mohair and other animal hair** (5102), wool waste and garnetted stock (5103–5104), **wool tops** and carded wool (5105), **wool and fine-hair yarn** (5106–5110) and **woollen and worsted fabric** (5111–5113). Of its **124 tariff lines, 29 are Free** — mostly coarse wool not finer than 46s — while finer wool pays a specific duty per **clean kilogram** (18.7¢–24.4¢), yarn 4%–6% and most wool fabric **25%**.

Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies also pay a **Section 301 tariff**: Peru, Chile, New Zealand, Australia, Uruguay and South Africa 12.5% on top of the base rate, the UK and India 10%, and **EU goods 10% in total** (EU fabric at 25% pays only its base rate). An FTA claim (Peru, Chile, Australia) removes the base rate but not this duty. **China pays 37.5%** extra on every line, Brazil 37.5%, and Canadian greasy fine wool and wool waste 50% under Section 338. U.S. imports were **$256.8M in 2025**, led by Peru (18%) and Italy (15%); yarn of 5106–5109 was 53% of the total — Peru's hand-knitting yarn of wool and fine hair (5109) alone $34.6M — and woven fabric of 5111–5112 38%.

productGroups.label: Wool, not carded or combed (greasy, scoured, carbonized)
productGroups.blurb: Greasy (shorn or skin wool), degreased and carbonized wool. Wool not finer than 46s — carpet and coarse wool — is Free; finer wool pays 18.7¢ (greasy), 20.6¢ (degreased) or 24.4¢ (carbonized) per clean kg, and 6.5¢/kg + 5.3% if processed further. "Wool for special uses" (felt, carpets, press cloth) is Free and, for Column 2 countries, Free only under bond. $9.3M in 2025, mostly from New Zealand $5.7M, Australia $1.4M.

productGroups.label: Fine or coarse animal hair, not carded or combed (cashmere, camel, alpaca, mohair)
productGroups.blurb: Cashmere, camel, alpaca, llama, vicuña, mohair, yak and rabbit hair, and coarse animal hair, not carded or combed. Degreased cashmere 5.1¢/clean kg, camel hair 5¢/clean kg, alpaca and mohair (5102.19.60) 0.4%, coarse hair Free. $6.0M in 2025, mostly from Belgium $3.8M, Portugal $1.1M.

productGroups.label: Waste of wool or of fine or coarse animal hair, including yarn waste and noils
productGroups.blurb: Noils, yarn waste and other waste of wool and fine animal hair (2.6¢/kg) and waste of coarse hair (7%). Garnetted (pulled) stock is 5104. $1.0M in 2025, mostly from Egypt $436K, United Kingdom $200K.

productGroups.label: Garnetted stock of wool or of fine or coarse animal hair
productGroups.blurb: Garnetted stock — wool or hair waste pulled back into fibre. Free; Column 2 57.3¢/kg. $292K in 2025, mostly from Belgium $235K, Canada $35K.

productGroups.label: Wool and fine or coarse animal hair, carded or combed (wool tops, combed wool in fragments)
productGroups.blurb: Carded wool, combed wool tops and combed wool in fragments, and carded or combed cashmere and other fine hair. Mixed rates of 3.7¢–6.8¢/kg plus 3%–5.5%; coarse hair Free. $5.3M in 2025, mostly from Uruguay $999K, Australia $940K.

productGroups.label: Yarn of carded wool, not put up for retail sale
productGroups.blurb: Woollen-spun (carded) wool yarn for weaving and knitting mills, 6%. The 85%-wool line is split at 34.40 microns for statistics. $15.0M in 2025, mostly from United Kingdom $3.1M, Denmark $2.6M.

productGroups.label: Yarn of combed wool, not put up for retail sale
productGroups.blurb: Worsted (combed) wool yarn, 6%, split at 18.5 microns (superfine merino) and at 85% wool. $48.0M in 2025, mostly from Mexico $12.1M, Canada $11.6M.

productGroups.label: Yarn of fine animal hair (carded or combed), not put up for retail sale
productGroups.blurb: Yarn of cashmere, camel, alpaca, mohair, Angora rabbit and other fine hair, not for retail sale: 4%. $17.9M in 2025, mostly from Peru $9.1M, Italy $4.6M.

productGroups.label: Yarn of wool or of fine animal hair, put up for retail sale
productGroups.blurb: Hand-knitting and retail wool and fine-hair yarn in balls, hanks or skeins: 6% wool, 4% Angora rabbit, Free for dyed yarn cut to 8 cm or less (rug yarn). $56.2M in 2025, mostly from Peru $34.6M, Italy $5.1M.

productGroups.label: Yarn of coarse animal hair or of horsehair (including gimped horsehair yarn)
productGroups.blurb: Yarn of coarse animal hair and of horsehair, including gimped horsehair yarn. Free. $245K in 2025, mostly from South Africa $139K, Peru $54K.

productGroups.label: Woven fabrics of carded wool or of carded fine animal hair (woollens)
productGroups.blurb: Woollen (carded) fabric — tweeds, flannels, coatings, melton. 25% for most lines; 7% tapestry and upholstery fabric; 10% hand-woven on narrow looms; 6.9% with 30% or more silk valued over $33/kg. $29.8M in 2025, mostly from United Kingdom $9.3M, Italy $8.0M.

productGroups.label: Woven fabrics of combed wool or of combed fine animal hair (worsteds)
productGroups.blurb: Worsted (combed) fabric — suitings, gabardine, crepe — 25% for most lines; 7% tapestry and upholstery; 6.9% with 30% or more silk over $33/kg. Fabric of 18.5-micron yarn and weights over 270 g/m² have their own statistical lines. $67.6M in 2025, mostly from Italy $18.3M, Chile $14.8M.

productGroups.label: Woven fabrics of coarse animal hair or of horsehair
productGroups.blurb: Woven fabric of coarse animal hair or horsehair (hair cloth, interlining). 2.7%. $303K in 2025, mostly from United Kingdom $107K, France $84K.

workedExamples.title: Greasy merino wool from Australia
workedExamples.body: Greasy shorn wool finer than 58s is 18.7¢ per clean kg. 20,000 kg greasy at a 65% clean yield is 13,000 clean kg: **$2,431** base duty. An Australia FTA claim (AU) removes it, but the 12.5% Section 301 duty (9903.05.23) still applies: **$12,500** on a $100,000 shipment, or $14,931 without the FTA claim.

workedExamples.title: Italian worsted suiting fabric
workedExamples.body: Worsted fabric of 18.5-micron wool up to 200 g/m² is 25%. EU goods pay 10% in total only where the base rate is lower (note 52(k)); here the 25% base rate applies alone: **$12,500** on $50,000. The same fabric from China pays 25% + 25% (List 3) + 12.5% = 62.5%: **$31,250**.

workedExamples.title: Worsted fabric from Chile
workedExamples.body: Worsted wool fabric of 270–340 g/m² is 25%. A Chile FTA claim (CL) makes it Free, and the 12.5% Section 301 duty (9903.05.30) still applies: **$2,500** on $20,000, against $7,500 without the claim.

workedExamples.title: Alpaca yarn from Peru
workedExamples.body: Combed fine-hair yarn is 4%. A Peru TPA claim (PE) makes it Free, and the 12.5% Section 301 duty (9903.05.63) still applies: **$1,250** on $10,000 ($1,650 without the PE claim).

workedExamples.title: Cashmere yarn: China vs. Mongolia
workedExamples.body: Carded cashmere yarn is 4%. From China it adds 25% (List 3, 9903.88.03) and 12.5% (9903.05.31): **$4,150** on $10,000. Mongolia is not one of the 60 Section 301 economies, so Mongolian yarn pays the 4% only: **$400**.

workedExamples.title: Greasy fine wool from Canada
workedExamples.body: Greasy wool not finer than 58s is 18.7¢/clean kg, Free with a USMCA claim, which also removes Canada's 10% Section 301 duty. But 5101.11.60 is on the Section 338 list (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14): **50%** applies with or without USMCA — $5,000 on $10,000.

workedExamples.title: Coarse carpet wool entered as "wool for special uses"
workedExamples.body: Wool not finer than 46s certified for felt, carpets, press cloth or papermakers' felts is Free at the general rate. For a Column 2 country the rate is "Free, under bond": duty-free at entry, but if the wool is used for anything else the regular duty (55.1¢–77.2¢/clean kg for greasy shorn wool) becomes payable (additional U.S. note 2(d)).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Throughout the tariff schedule: (a) **"wool"** is the natural fibre grown by sheep or lambs; (b) **"fine animal hair"** is the hair of alpaca, llama, vicuña, camel (including dromedary), yak, Angora, Tibetan, Kashmir or similar goats (but not common goats), rabbit (including Angora rabbit), hare, beaver, nutria or muskrat; and (c) **"coarse animal hair"** is the hair of other animals, excluding brush-making hair and bristles (heading 0502) and horsehair (heading 0511). Horsehair itself is chapter 5; only its yarn (5110) and woven fabric (5113) are here.

The Section XI (textiles) notes also apply: a blend is classified as if it consisted wholly of the fibre that predominates by weight (wool and fine animal hair counted together), and fabric cut to shape or hemmed leaves Chapter 51 for chapters 61–63.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**Note 1.** In a package of wool or fine hair at different rates (headings 5101–5104), the whole package takes the highest rate applying to any part that is at least 10% of the contents by weight.

**Note 2(a)–(c).** **"Clean kg"** means kilogram of clean yield: the absolute clean content (wool or hair free of vegetable and foreign matter, at 12% moisture, 1.5% alcohol-extractable matter and not over 0.5% ash), less an allowance for normal processing loss. For carbonized fibre, clean yield is the condition as entered. CBP samples and tests clean yield under 19 CFR 151.61–151.76.

**Note 2(d) — wool for special uses.** Unimproved wool and other wool not finer than 46s, entered by a dealer, manufacturer or processor and certified for use only in felt or knit boots, floor coverings, heavy fulled lumbermen's socks, press cloth, papermakers' felts or pressed felt for polishing plate and mirror glass. It is not released without a **bond** securing that use; it can be transferred to another bonded user. If it is used or transferred for any other use, the regular duty on the wool in its condition as entered must be paid (not on waste or by-products of the permitted manufacture, or on goods destroyed or exported); misuse must be reported within 30 days or a penalty equal to the wool's value applies; and clean yield is deemed 100% unless tested and used within 3 years of entry. In the current schedule this matters for **Column 2** countries ("Free, under bond" on 5101.11.10, 5101.19.10, 5101.21.10 and 5101.29.10); at the general rate all wool not finer than 46s is Free anyway.

**Note 2(e)–(f).** "Unimproved wool" is Aleppo, Chinese, Donskoi, Karakul, Mongolian, Scotch Blackface, Tibetan, Welsh Mountain and similar wool not improved by merino or English blood. Wool grades follow the U.S. standards set by the Secretary of Agriculture in force on the date of import.

**No wool-fabric quota.** The worsted wool fabric tariff-rate quotas that once lowered the duty on some 5112 suitings are no longer in the schedule: Commerce removed their regulations in 2019 because the authority had expired, and Chapter 99 of Revision 21 has no heading that lowers the duty on 5111 or 5112 fabric. The temporary duty suspensions for cashmere, camel hair and vicuña (9902.12.69–9902.12.82) expired December 31, 2020.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 51 wool, hair, yarn and fabric imports since January 2025: unchanged base rates, the end of the IEEPA tariffs and the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on Australia, Peru, the EU and others, China's List 3 and Canada's Section 338 duty on wool.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 124 Chapter 51 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies — Peru, Chile, the UK, the EU, India, Türkiye and New Zealand among them — pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**. China keeps its 25% List 3 duty on every Chapter 51 line, Brazil pays another 25%, and since August 22, 2026 Canadian greasy fine wool (5101.11.60) and wool waste (5103.20) pay **50%** under Section 338.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 51 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exception lists, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 3, the Canada Section 338 duty, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. No Section 232 action and no antidumping or countervailing duty order covers a Chapter 51 line; the only past order, a countervailing duty on wool from Argentina, was revoked in 1997. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: Peru has no exception list. A Peru TPA claim (PE) removes the base rate on every dutiable line but not this duty (note 52(a)). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Peruvian yarn of wool and fine hair ($47.2M in 2025) — mostly hand-knitting yarn of 5109 — pays 12.5% with a PE claim, and the 4%–6% base rate on top without one.

inEffect.exemption: EU goods pay 10% in total in place of a lower base rate (U.S. note 52(k)); where the base rate is 10% or more — the 25% woollen and worsted fabric lines — only the base rate applies. The EU exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(2), 9903.05.97) names no Chapter 51 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Italian, German and other EU worsted and woollen fabric pays its 25% base rate and nothing more; EU yarn (4%–6%) and wool pay 10% in total.

inEffect.exemption: The UK exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(1), 9903.05.96) names no Chapter 51 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: British worsted and tweed fabric and yarn ($25.9M in 2025) pay the base rate plus 10%: 35% on 25% fabric.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94); goods must meet the General Note 11 rules of origin for Chapter 51. The 2025 IEEPA duty on Mexico (+25%, 9903.01.01) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Mexican worsted yarn and fabric ($25.1M in 2025) pay $0 extra with a valid USMCA claim and 10% without one.

inEffect.exemption: Chile has no exception list. A Chile FTA claim (CL) removes the base rate on every dutiable line but not this duty (note 52(a)). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chilean worsted fabric ($14.9M in 2025) — almost all of 5112 — is Free with a CL claim but pays 12.5%: $1,250 on $10,000 instead of $2,500 at the 25% base rate.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), but the 50% Section 338 duty (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14) on greasy shorn wool finer than 46s (5101.11.60) and other waste of wool or fine hair (5103.20) applies with or without a USMCA claim; both stayed on the list after the September 15, 2026 revision. No Chapter 51 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes. The IEEPA duty on Canada ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian worsted yarn and other goods ($13.1M in 2025) pay nothing extra with USMCA, except 50% on greasy fine wool of 5101.11.60 and wool waste of 5103.20 (60% without a USMCA claim).

inEffect.exemption: India has no exception list. GSP (SPI A), printed on four Chapter 51 lines, has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties (25% reciprocal plus 25% over Russian oil purchases) ended in February 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian wool yarn and fabric ($8.0M in 2025) pay 10% on top of the base rate.

inEffect.exemption: Türkiye has no exception list for Chapter 51. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Turkish wool yarn and fabric ($7.8M in 2025) pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: New Zealand has no FTA with the United States and no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: New Zealand wool ($7.6M in 2025) — much of it coarse wool not finer than 46s, Free at the base rate — pays 12.5% extra.

inEffect.exemption: List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03, 25% since May 10, 2019) covers all 101 Chapter 51 subheadings, and the 2026 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31); China is on no exception list. The exclusions once granted for Merino wool yarn (5106.10.0090) and cashmere yarn (5108.10.8000) have lapsed, and none of the exclusions still in force (9903.88.69–9903.88.70, through November 9, 2026) names a Chapter 51 product. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018–2019 actions continue. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese cashmere, wool tops, yarn and fabric pay 37.5% on top of the base rate: 41.5% on 4% cashmere yarn, 62.5% on 25% wool fabric.

inEffect.exemption: Australia has no exception list, and the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) names no Chapter 51 code. An Australia FTA claim (AU) removes the base rate on the dutiable lines (fine wool, tops, yarn, fabric) but not this duty (note 52(a)). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Australian greasy and scoured wool, tops and yarn pay 12.5% on top of the base rate — 12.5% in all with an FTA claim.

inEffect.exemption: South Africa has no exception list. AGOA (SPI D, through December 31, 2026 for beneficiary countries) is printed only on 5102.19.60 (mohair, alpaca), 5103.10, 5103.20 and 5113.00, and does not remove this duty. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: South African mohair and wool pay the base rate plus 12.5% — 12.9% on mohair of 5102.19.60 without an AGOA claim.

inEffect.exemption: Uruguay has no FTA with the United States and no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Uruguayan wool tops and scoured wool pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Brazil's 25% (9903.05.01, from July 22, 2026) reaches every Chapter 51 line; its exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03) names no Chapter 51 code. The 2026 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.27). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian wool and hair pay 37.5% on top of the base rate.

inEffect.exemption: Japanese goods pay 12.5% in total in place of a lower base rate (note 52(k)); the 25% fabric lines pay their base rate only. Japan has no exception list naming Chapter 51. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Japanese wool fabric pays its 25% base rate; yarn and fibre pay 12.5% in total.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (including Argentina, Switzerland, South Korea, Taiwan, Jordan, Guatemala and El Salvador)
inEffect.now: +10% or 10% (in place of base) or +12.5% or 12.5% (in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: Exception lists in U.S. note 52(j) reach Chapter 51 for: Jordan (5102.11.90, 5102.19.20 and every subheading of 5104–5113, 9903.06.20); Guatemala and El Salvador (5104–5113 when entered under CAFTA-DR, 9903.06.06 and 9903.06.09); Cambodia (5102.11.90 and 5102.19.20, 9903.06.02); Taiwan and Switzerland (5102.11.90, 9903.06.14 and 9903.05.98). CAFTA-DR textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free with a CAFTA-DR claim (SPI P/P+) are exempt on 5105–5113 except 5105.40 (note 52(i), 9903.05.95); raw wool, hair and waste of 5101–5104 are not covered, and lines already Free at the general rate carry no P rate to claim. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most other suppliers pay the base rate plus 10% or 12.5%; Taiwan pays 10% in total, and countries outside the 60 economies — Mongolia, for example — pay only the base rate.

changes.title: No Chapter 51 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 124 Chapter 51 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018–2019 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 51 this keeps +25% (List 3, 9903.88.03) on all 101 subheadings.

changes.title: Canadian import bans do not reach Chapter 51
changes.detail: Proclamations 11061–11063 banned some Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy-scope products and motor vehicles from September 29, 2026. No Chapter 51 line is on their annexes.

changes.title: Section 338 list revised; wool lines stay on it
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 added and deleted products on the 9903.03.14 list from September 15, 2026. Neither Chapter 51 provision (5101.11.60, 5103.20.00) was removed; Revision 21 still lists both in U.S. note 51(b)(3).

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty of 50% on greasy fine wool and wool waste
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on Canadian goods in the provisions of U.S. note 51(b)(3), which include greasy shorn wool finer than 46s (5101.11.60) and other waste of wool or fine animal hair (5103.20.00). It is charged even when USMCA is claimed and on top of the 10% Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods. Planned for August 19, it took effect August 22 after a 3-day suspension (Proclamation 11056).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies reach every Chapter 51 line
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84); no Chapter 51 subheading is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Peru, Chile, New Zealand, Australia, Uruguay, South Africa and Türkiye pay 12.5%; the UK, India and Argentina 10%; EU goods 10% in total and Japanese, Korean and Swiss goods 12.5% in total. Jordan's list, the Guatemala and El Salvador CAFTA-DR lists (5104–5113) and single-line lists for Cambodia, Taiwan and Switzerland (processed cashmere) exempt some Chapter 51 goods. USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94), and so are CAFTA-DR textile goods of 5105–5113 (not 5105.40) entered duty-free with a P/P+ claim (note 52(i), 9903.05.95); AU, PE, CL and other FTA claims remove the base rate but not this duty.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 51 subheading is on Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 51 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08).

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. India's 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75) renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025. AGOA (SPI D) is printed on four Chapter 51 lines — mohair, alpaca and other hair of 5102.19.60, noils (5103.10), other wool waste (5103.20) and horsehair fabric (5113.00). GSP (SPI A), printed on the same lines, remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty on all Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches every Chapter 51 line.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It applied to every Chapter 51 line on top of the List 3 duty until it ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) over India's purchases of Russian oil, on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025 (EO 14326): 50% in all. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 replaced the 10% baseline with country rates, for example New Zealand +15%, South Africa +30%, India +25%, Türkiye +15%, while Peru, Chile, Australia, Uruguay and the UK stayed at +10%, and EU and Japanese goods paid 15% in total. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 (signed July 30, 2025) added 40% on goods of Brazil, on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 51 subheading was on the general exemption list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the 25% List 3 duty on cashmere, tops, yarn and fabric.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Worsted wool fabric tariff-rate quotas end
changes.detail: Commerce removed its regulations for the worsted wool fabric tariff-rate quotas of the Trade and Development Act of 2000 because the quota authority had expired. Revision 21 has no Chapter 99 heading lowering the duty on 5111 or 5112 fabric, so worsted suitings pay the full 25% base rate.

changes.title: Countervailing duty order on wool from Argentina revoked
changes.detail: Commerce revoked the countervailing duty order on wool from Argentina after a changed-circumstances review. No antidumping or countervailing duty order has covered Chapter 51 goods since.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 51 goods were **$256.8M in 2025**, up 4.5% from $245.8M in 2024, against a peak of $283.9M in 2022. **Peru shipped $47.2M (18%)**, then **Italy** $38.8M (+20%), **United Kingdom** $25.9M (+15%), **Mexico** $25.1M (-8%), **Chile** $14.9M (+39%), **Canada** $13.1M (-23%).

By product, the largest were **worsted fabric** (5112) $67.6M (26%), **retail yarn** (5109) $56.2M (22%), **worsted yarn** (5107) $48.0M (19%), **woollen fabric** (5111) $29.8M (12%). Yarn of 5106–5109 was $137.0M (53%) in all: retail yarn mostly from Peru $34.6M, Italy $5.1M, worsted yarn from Mexico $12.1M, Canada $11.6M, Romania $5.7M. Worsted fabric came from Italy $18.3M, Chile $14.8M, United Kingdom $7.5M, woollen fabric from United Kingdom $9.3M, Italy $8.0M. Fibre, waste and tops (5101–5105) were only $21.9M; raw wool came mostly from New Zealand $5.7M, Australia $1.4M.

Through 2025 most suppliers paid the IEEPA tariffs on top of the base rate, and China its 25% List 3 duty as well. The IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies to most of these suppliers instead. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
The total rate on Chapter 51 goods depends on **what they are and where they come from**. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026). **Peruvian** yarn and **Chilean** worsted fabric are Free with an FTA claim but pay 12.5%; **British** fabric pays 25% plus 10%; **Italian and other EU fabric** pays only its 25% base rate (EU goods pay 10% in total where the base rate is lower); **China and Brazil pay 37.5% more** on every line, and Canadian greasy fine wool and wool waste pay 50% under Section 338 even with USMCA. Wool rates per clean kilogram are shown as written.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Wool, Cashmere & Alpaca (HTS Ch. 51): Clean Yield, APHIS, Labeling & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Wool & Cashmere: Clean-Yield Testing, APHIS Wool Rules, Wool Labeling Act & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 51) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The CBP, USDA APHIS, FWS and FTC rules for each HTS Chapter 51 line — clean-yield sampling and wool grading (19 CFR 151), APHIS foot-and-mouth disease rules for raw wool and hair (9 CFR 95), vicuña permits, textile origin and the Wool Products Labeling Act (16 CFR 300) — and the legal ways to pay less.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Raw wool is the one textile CBP charges by **clean weight**: invoices must give the condition, grade and estimated clean yield of each lot, and CBP samples and lab-tests it before liquidating the duty (19 CFR 151.61–151.76). **APHIS** lets wool and hair in without restriction only if it comes from a region free of foot-and-mouth disease, was clipped from live animals, was scoured or dyed, or carries a slaughter certificate; otherwise it goes under seal to an approved establishment (9 CFR 95.18–95.19). Vicuña needs CITES labels, and wool yarns and fabrics sold on must be labeled under the **Wool Products Labeling Act** — "cashmere" only if 19 microns or finer.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: claim the **Australia or Peru FTA** or **USMCA**, use the **Jordan or CAFTA-DR exception lists**, enter coarse wool as **wool for special uses**, get the **classification** right where fineness, processing or weave moves the rate, enter **samples** under Chapter 98, and claim **drawback** on re-exports.

levers.title: Claim the Australia, Peru or another FTA rate on the dutiable lines
levers.saves: The base rate: 18.7¢–24.4¢ per clean kg on fine wool, 4%–6% on yarn, 25% on most wool fabric
levers.appliesTo: The 95 dutiable lines, for goods of Australia, Peru, Korea, Chile, Colombia, Panama, Israel, Jordan, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman, Singapore and CAFTA-DR countries; CBERA (E) on the fibre lines; AGOA (D, through December 31, 2026) on 5102.19.60, 5103.10, 5103.20 and 5113.00
levers.document: Proof of origin under the agreement and the SPI on the entry line (AU, PE, KR, CL, CO, PA, IL, JO, MA, BH, OM, SG, P, E, D).
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)), except CAFTA-DR textile goods of 5105–5113 (not 5105.40) entered duty-free with a P/P+ claim (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). GSP (A) has been expired since December 31, 2020.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a), (i)

levers.title: Claim USMCA on wool, yarn or fabric made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty for Mexico or Canada plus the base rate (up to 25%)
levers.appliesTo: All 124 lines, for goods that qualify as originating under General Note 11 (Chapter 51 product-specific rules of origin)
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format, with the SPI "S" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on greasy fine wool (5101.11.60) and wool waste (5103.20). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.title: Use an exception list or CAFTA-DR: Jordan, the six CAFTA-DR countries, or processed cashmere from Switzerland, Taiwan or Cambodia
levers.appliesTo: Jordan: 5102.11.90, 5102.19.20 and all of 5104–5113 (9903.06.20); Guatemala and El Salvador under CAFTA-DR: 5104–5113 (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09); any CAFTA-DR country entering 5105–5113 (not 5105.40) duty-free with a P/P+ claim (note 52(i), 9903.05.95); Cambodia: 5102.11.90 and 5102.19.20 (9903.06.02); Taiwan and Switzerland: 5102.11.90 (9903.06.14, 9903.05.98)
levers.document: Proof of origin for the country claimed (invoice, manufacturer ID, production records), the exemption heading on the entry line, and for CAFTA-DR the SPI "P" claim.
levers.caveat: Raw and scoured wool of 5101 is on no exception list. Origin follows 19 CFR 102.21: yarn is from where it was spun and fabric from where it was woven.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(i), (j)

levers.title: Enter coarse carpet and felting wool as "wool for special uses"
levers.saves: For Column 2 origins, 55.1¢–81.6¢ per clean kg on wool not finer than 46s; at the general rate this wool is Free anyway
levers.appliesTo: 5101.11.10, 5101.19.10, 5101.21.10 and 5101.29.10: wool not finer than 46s, certified for felt or knit boots, floor coverings, lumbermen's socks, press cloth, papermakers' felts or polishing felt
levers.document: A dealer, manufacturer or processor certification of the special use and a bond; transfers only to another bonded user; misuse reported within 30 days.
levers.caveat: If the wool is used otherwise, the regular duty on it in its condition as entered becomes payable, and the Section 301 duty still applies to the country's goods (Russia 12.5%).

levers.title: Get a binding ruling where fineness, processing or weave decides the rate
levers.saves: Up to 25 points: 46s and coarser wool (Free) vs. finer wool (18.7¢+/clean kg); degreased vs. further processed (6.5¢/kg + 5.3%); fine animal hair (yarn 4%) vs. wool (6%); upholstery fabric (7%) vs. apparel fabric (25%); 30% silk over $33/kg (6.9%); hand-woven narrow-loom fabric (10%)
levers.appliesTo: Any line where wool grade, fibre blend, fabric use or weight is in doubt — especially wool–cashmere and wool–synthetic blends, which follow the fibre that predominates by weight (Section XI note 2)
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing fibre content by weight, micron and grade, construction, weight in g/m² and end use (19 CFR part 177); invoices must state the same details (19 CFR 141.89, 151.62).
levers.caveat: Grades follow USDA standards in force on the date of import (additional U.S. note 2(f)), and CBP examines wool for grade (19 CFR 151.76).

levers.title: Enter fabric swatches and yarn cards as samples
levers.saves: All duty — base rate and the Section 301 and China duties
levers.appliesTo: Wool fabric swatches and yarn samples valued at $1 or less each, or marked, torn or perforated so they cannot be sold, used only to solicit orders
levers.document: Entry under 9811.00.60 with the samples marked or mutilated as the heading requires.
levers.caveat: Usable sample lengths do not qualify. U.S. notes 20 and 52 exempt goods properly entered under Chapter 98 from those extra duties; the Canada Section 338 duty also excludes most Chapter 98 entries.

provisions.text: Samples valued not over $1 each, or marked, torn, perforated or otherwise treated so they are unsuitable for sale, used only for soliciting orders for products of foreign countries

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20(a), 51(a), 52(a)

levers.title: Claim drawback when the wool, yarn or fabric, or what it is made into, is exported
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on imported goods re-exported or used in exported goods
levers.appliesTo: All lines, when the imported goods or substitutes are exported or used in manufacturing exported goods
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; manufacturing drawback needs a ruling or a general manufacturing ruling.

rules.title: Wool and hair dutiable per clean kilogram: invoices must show condition, vegetable-matter level, length, origin, grade and the shipper's clean-yield estimate; the entry summary shows estimated clean kilograms; CBP weighs, samples and lab-tests each sampling unit, and the importer may ask for a retest and a commercial test
Wool dutiable per clean kilogram is examined for grade against the USDA wool standards in force on the date of import; a higher grade than entered means a higher rate
Wool for special uses (not finer than 46s) is released only under a bond securing its use in felt, carpets, press cloth or papermakers' felts; other use makes the regular duty payable

Wool and hair of ruminants: unrestricted entry if from a region free of foot-and-mouth disease, clipped from live animals and reasonably free of dung, scoured, washed or dyed, or certified as from inspected slaughter; otherwise moved under seal to an approved establishment and handled under inspection. Bloodstained wool or hair is prohibited

Vicuña: only wool sheared from live animals of CITES Appendix II populations, and cloth and products from it, may be imported, with the vicuña logotype and "VICUÑA—COUNTRY OF ORIGIN" on the selvages; wildlife imports are declared to FWS

Textile country of origin: raw wool and hair from where shorn or obtained; scouring, carding or combing do not shift origin (5101–5103 and 5105 need a change from another chapter); yarn from where it was spun; fabric from where it was woven
Manufacturer identification code (MID) of the company that performed the origin-conferring operation on every entry; entry is denied for textiles from companies named by CITA for transshipment
Invoice details for yarn and fabric: fibre content by weight with each fibre's generic name and percentage, and for fabric the construction, weight per m² and finish that pick the 10-digit line

Wool Products Labeling Act: wool yarns, fabrics and products sold onward must show fibre content and the country where processed or made; "cashmere" only for fibre averaging 19 microns or less, and "Super 100s"-type terms only at the listed fibre diameters
UFLPA: goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are presumed made with forced labor and excluded unless the importer rebuts it
Country-of-origin marking on the article or, for bales of wool and piece goods, on the container

groups.label: Wool, not carded or combed (greasy, scoured, carbonized)
groups.note: Duty per clean kg on wool finer than 46s, set after CBP tests clean yield and grade. APHIS: unrestricted only from FMD-free regions, if clipped from live animals, or if scoured.

groups.label: Fine or coarse animal hair, not carded or combed (cashmere, camel, alpaca, mohair)
groups.note: Cashmere and camel hair pay per clean kg; alpaca and mohair 0.4%. Vicuña fibre needs CITES labeling; processed cashmere (5102.11.90) is on the Jordan, Swiss, Taiwanese and Cambodian exception lists.

groups.label: Waste of wool or of fine or coarse animal hair, including yarn waste and noils
groups.note: Noils and other wool waste: Canada's 5103.20 pays the 50% Section 338 duty even with USMCA.

groups.label: Garnetted stock of wool or of fine or coarse animal hair
groups.note: Garnetted stock is Free; recycled-wool content must be disclosed on wool labels.

groups.label: Wool and fine or coarse animal hair, carded or combed (wool tops, combed wool in fragments)
groups.note: Combing tops from imported greasy wool does not change origin under the tariff-shift rule; get a ruling before relying on the combing country.

groups.label: Yarn of carded wool, not put up for retail sale
groups.note: Woollen yarn takes the origin of the spinning country. 6%; on the Jordan and CAFTA-DR exception lists.

groups.label: Yarn of combed wool, not put up for retail sale
groups.note: Worsted yarn takes the origin of the spinning country. 6%; the 18.5-micron split is statistical only.

groups.label: Yarn of fine animal hair (carded or combed), not put up for retail sale
groups.note: Cashmere, alpaca and mohair yarn, 4%. Labels may say "cashmere" only for fibre of 19 microns or less.

groups.label: Yarn of wool or of fine animal hair, put up for retail sale
groups.note: Retail hand-knitting yarn, 6% wool, 4% Angora; dyed rug yarn cut to 8 cm or less is Free.

groups.label: Yarn of coarse animal hair or of horsehair (including gimped horsehair yarn)
groups.note: Horsehair yarn is Free; raw horsehair is heading 0511, not Chapter 51.

groups.label: Woven fabrics of carded wool or of carded fine animal hair (woollens)
groups.note: Woollen fabric takes the origin of the weaving country. 25% apparel fabric vs. 7% upholstery: classification follows the fabric as entered.

groups.label: Woven fabrics of combed wool or of combed fine animal hair (worsteds)
groups.note: Worsted fabric takes the origin of the weaving country. "Super 120s" and similar labels must meet 16 CFR 300.20a.

groups.note: Horsehair and coarse-hair fabric, 2.7%; AGOA (D) Free for beneficiary countries.

seo.title: Wool, Cashmere & Alpaca HS Code and Tariff FAQ 2026: Wool Yarn, Wool Fabric, Mohair (HTS Chapter 51) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about importing Chapter 51 goods: the HS code for wool, wool yarn, wool fabric, cashmere, alpaca, mohair and horsehair, and the 2026 tariffs on wool from Australia, Peru, Italy, the UK and China.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing wool, cashmere, alpaca, mohair and wool yarn and fabric into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 51 base rates are unchanged since January 2025: wool not finer than 46s is Free, finer wool 18.7¢–24.4¢ per clean kg, yarn 4%–6%, and most woollen and worsted fabric 25%.
Since July 24, 2026 most suppliers pay a 10% or 12.5% Section 301 tariff — Peru, Chile, New Zealand and Australia 12.5% even with an FTA claim, the UK 10%; EU fabric pays only its 25% base rate.
China and Brazil pay 37.5% extra on every line; Canadian greasy fine wool and wool waste pay 50% under Section 338 even with USMCA.
The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. There is no wool-fabric quota and no antidumping or countervailing duty on Chapter 51 goods.
Raw wool is dutied on CBP-tested clean yield and needs APHIS clearance; wool yarn and fabric follow textile origin rules and the Wool Products Labeling Act.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for raw wool?
faqs.answer: Raw wool, not carded or combed, is heading 5101: greasy shorn wool 5101.11, other greasy (skin) wool 5101.19, degreased (scoured) wool 5101.21 and 5101.29, carbonized wool 5101.30. Each splits by fineness: wool not finer than 46s is Free, finer merino-type wool pays 18.7¢ (greasy), 20.6¢ (scoured) or 24.4¢ (carbonized) per clean kg. Wool tops are 5105.29.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for wool fabric?
faqs.answer: Woven wool fabric is 5111 if made of carded (woollen) yarn and 5112 if of combed (worsted) yarn, split by weight and blend. Most apparel lines are 25%; tapestry and upholstery fabric 7%; hand-woven fabric on looms under 76 cm 10%; fabric with 30% or more silk valued over $33/kg 6.9%. Knitted wool fabric is chapter 60, and poly-wool fabric is Chapter 51 only if wool predominates by weight.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for wool yarn and merino wool yarn?
faqs.answer: Wool yarn for mills is 5106 (carded, woollen-spun) or 5107 (combed, worsted), both 6%; 5107.10.30 and 5107.20.30 are for yarn of 18.5 microns or finer. Hand-knitting yarn put up for retail sale is 5109 (6%).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for cashmere, and are cashmere sweaters and scarves in Chapter 51?
faqs.answer: Raw cashmere is 5102.11 (5.1¢/clean kg degreased, 4.9¢/kg + 4% if processed further), carded or combed cashmere 5105.31, cashmere yarn 5108 (4%) and woven cashmere fabric 5111–5112. Sweaters are heading 6110 and scarves 6117 or 6214 — not Chapter 51. Chinese cashmere yarn pays 41.5% in all; Mongolian pays 4%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for alpaca fibre and alpaca yarn?
faqs.answer: Alpaca fibre not processed beyond the degreased condition is 5102.19.60 (0.4%; 5102.19.90 if processed further), alpaca tops 5105.39, and alpaca yarn 5108 (4%) or 5109 if put up for retail sale. From Peru, a Peru TPA claim removes the base rate but the 12.5% Section 301 duty (9903.05.63) applies. Alpaca sweaters are heading 6110.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for mohair?
faqs.answer: Mohair (hair of the Angora goat) is 5102.19.60.30 (0.4%; Free under AGOA for beneficiary countries), mohair yarn 5108.10.40 or 5108.20.40 (4%), and woven mohair fabric 5111 or 5112. Angora rabbit hair is a different line (yarn 5108.x0.30).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for horsehair?
faqs.answer: Raw horsehair is heading 0511 (chapter 5), not Chapter 51. Horsehair yarn, including gimped horsehair yarn, is 5110.00.00 (Free), and woven horsehair fabric 5113.00.00 (2.7%).

faqs.question: What is the tariff on wool in 2026?
faqs.answer: The base rate (Free to 25%) plus the extra duty by country. Since July 24, 2026 the Section 301 tariff on 60 economies adds 10% or 12.5% (EU goods 10% in total where the base rate is lower), China pays 37.5% and Brazil 37.5%, and Canadian greasy fine wool and wool waste 50%. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026.

faqs.question: Is raw wool from Australia and New Zealand duty-free?
faqs.answer: Not since July 24, 2026. Coarse wool not finer than 46s is Free at the base rate, and the Australia FTA makes finer Australian wool Free too, but both countries now pay the 12.5% Section 301 duty (9903.05.23, 9903.05.57). New Zealand has no FTA, so its fine wool also pays 18.7¢–24.4¢ per clean kg.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on wool from the UK?
faqs.answer: British goods pay the base rate plus 10% (9903.05.81); the UK exception list names no Chapter 51 code. Worsted or tweed fabric at 25% pays 35% in all, wool yarn 16%.

faqs.question: What is the import duty on Italian wool fabric?
searchedAs: italy import duty on worsted wool
faqs.answer: Italian worsted and woollen fabric pays its 25% base rate and nothing more: EU goods pay 10% in total only where the base rate is lower (9903.05.39, note 52(k)). Italian wool yarn (6%) and tops pay 10% in total. The EU exception list names no Chapter 51 code.

faqs.question: What does "per clean kg" mean for wool duty?
faqs.answer: Kilograms of clean yield: the wool content free of grease, dirt and vegetable matter at 12% moisture, less an allowance for processing loss (Chapter 51 additional U.S. note 2). The entry states an estimate; CBP samples, lab-tests and grades the wool and liquidates on the final clean yield (19 CFR 151.61–151.76).

faqs.question: What does the Wool Products Labeling Act require for imported wool?
faqs.answer: Wool yarns, fabrics and products sold in the U.S. must be labeled with fibre content by percentage and the country where processed or made (16 CFR 300.3, 300.25). "Cashmere" may be used only for fibre averaging 19 microns or less with no more than 3% over 30 microns, and "Super 100s"-type terms only at set fibre diameters.

faqs.question: Do wool fabric samples and swatches pay duty?
faqs.answer: Swatches worth $1 or less each, or marked, torn or perforated so they cannot be sold, used only to solicit orders, can enter Free under 9811.00.60, which also takes them outside the Section 301 and China duties. Usable sample lengths are classified in 5111 or 5112 like any other fabric.
